subject: Residency & subprocessor evidence: where requests are executed
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@seqrahealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency & Subprocessor Questions for Redwood Eval

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the demo last week — Seqra is evaluating Redwood for a pilot in our clinical triage product. Before we proceed we need a concise summary of where data is processed and who touches it. Our security checklist specifically asks: which regions/processors can you guarantee, a current subprocessor roster, and evidence of deletion (SLOs) plus how cross-border routing is handled.

I've attached our intake questionnaire (seqra_compliance_request_v1.pdf). High level: if we keep data in the US, can you confirm that inference execution and any transient storage remain within US regions unless we explicitly opt-in to multi-region routing? Also: do you (or your subprocessors) ever persist payloads to long-term object storage outside the execution region?

Appreciate if you can reply with the short answers and a pointer to any evidence pack (SOC2 report, subproc snapshot). If helpful we can schedule a 30m follow-up with our security team.

Best,
Emma
Emma Jones
Head of IT Security | Seqra Health

Attachment: seqra_compliance_request_v1.pdf (PDF, 124KB)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.example.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@seqrahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency & Subprocessor Questions for Redwood Eval

Emma — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes, we can run inference within a pinned region (e.g., US-West) and avoid cross-border execution by configuration; transient caching may occur on the serving nodes but we do not persist customer payloads to long-term object storage by default; we provide deletion APIs and a 48-hour deletion SLO for hosted API payloads unless the customer elects longer retention for debugging.

I'm looping Laura (technical PM, infra) for the subprocessor / evidence packet and a brief written snapshot of where requests physically execute. Laura, can you attach the current subprocessor snapshot and a one-page note on routing fallbacks and KMS usage?

If Seqra wants organizational isolation we can discuss Dedicated or Private deployments during the call. Happy to book a 30m slot — what times on Tuesday look good for you?

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@seqrahealth.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.example.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency & Subprocessor Questions for Redwood Eval

Emma — hi, Laura here from Platform. I pulled together the precise points you asked for and attached a short snapshot (redwood_subproc_snapshot_Jun2026.pdf). Key details below (summary, then specifics):

Summary:
- Execution regions: hosted API supports region pinning to AWS/us-west-2 (Oregon) and AWS/us-east-1 (N. Virginia) today, with eu-west-1 and asia-southeast-1 available for EU/APAC customers.
- Subprocessors: core compute and ephemeral caching run on AWS EC2 (operator-managed), object storage for customer-uploaded artifacts uses S3 (region-bound by config); telemetry/traces go to an internal observability cluster (managed on AWS but obfuscated); CDN edge (optional) via Cloudflare for specific features. We engage third-party model-ops partners for model compilation/quantization in isolated build environments — these are contractual subprocessors and appear in the snapshot.
- Cross-border routing: Default routing keeps requests in-region; smart routing policies (by customer config) can route to alternate regions for cost/latency; when routing fails we fall back to configured compatible model variant in the nearest allowed region (we never route outside an allowed geography if customer has geography pinning enabled).
- Retention & deletion: Hosted API retention defaults to 30 days for short-term debugging traces and 0 days for user payloads unless opt-in. Deletion via API triggers asynchronous erase; typical completion within 48 hours for hosted. Dedicated/Private customers can control retention SLOs and may opt for 0 retention.
- Evidence & controls: we hold a current SOC 2 Type II report (available under NDA), maintain KMS-encrypted access keys for data at rest, and keep audit logs including token-level access for 365 days (configurable for enterprise).

Specific subprocessors (summary list):
- Amazon Web Services, Inc. — EC2, S3 (region-bound)
- Cloudflare, Inc. — optional edge/CDN
- HashiCorp Cloud Vault (managed offering) — secrets store for hosted customers
- Model packaging partner: QuantifyAI Inc. — build-time model ops (no customer payloads retained)
- Monitoring provider: Observly Inc. — telemetry aggregation (scrubbed PII; customer identifiers only)

Attachments included: redwood_subproc_snapshot_Jun2026.pdf (contains contractual jurisdiction clauses and datacenter region map).

Technical notes:
- We use KMS keys scoped per-tenant in Dedicated/Private; hosted customers may use our managed KMS or bring-your-own in Private deployments.
- Transient KV caches (LLM KV caches) live in the serving process memory or ephemeral NVMe; nothing is written to long-term object storage unless the customer uploads artifacts.
- For customers requiring strict US-only execution we recommend Dedicated capacity in a US region or Private deployment; for hosted customers we can apply geography-pinning and additional contractual guarantees.

I'll attach the snapshot and the redacted SOC2 access instructions (NDA). Nikhil — happy to join the call if Emma's team wants deeper technical Q&A.

Laura Bennett
Technical PM, Platform | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subproc_snapshot_Jun2026.pdf (PDF, 78KB)
